title: System startup and shutdown history
description: List every system startup (EventID 6005) and shutdown (EventID 6006) event.

windowsCommandTemplate.name: Get-WinEvent
windowsCommandTemplate.commandPattern: Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=6005,6006,1074; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddDays(-{days})} | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,Message | Format-Table -AutoSize

parameters.name: days
parameters.label: Number of days
parameters.description: Number of days to look back

examples.description: Fast way to filter the errors (Level=2) of the last 24 hours. Much faster than Get-EventLog on large logs.

Show the last 100 events of the System log. Get-WinEvent is the modern cmdlet (it replaces Get-EventLog). -MaxEvents limits the results. It reads the classic logs AND the newer Applications and Services logs. Faster and more flexible than Get-EventLog.

List ALL the event logs available on the system. Returns the name, maximum size, record count and status (enabled or disabled). There can be hundreds of logs (System, Application, Security + all the Applications and Services logs). Use this command to discover the available logs.

Show the events of the PowerShell log. Applications and Services logs have path-like names (slashes). This log records all PowerShell activity: commands run, errors, scripts. Essential for security audits and PowerShell troubleshooting.

notes: EventID 6005 = Event Log service started, 6006 = Event Log service stopped, 1074 = shutdown initiated by a user or an application.

fr.notes: EventID 6005 = démarrage Event Log service, 6006 = arrêt Event Log service, 1074 = arrêt initié par utilisateur/application.
